protocol.primary: Captured-correct to restored-wrong transition in majority-speaking answer
protocol.secondary: Timestamped-tag errors, abstentions, and coverage across the same full 24 timestamps
protocol.safeguard: Separate restored condition with access to captured measurements for comparison
protocol.fixed: Source, interval, original audio, model, prompts, current-evidence tool schema, and evaluation labels
protocol.changed_primary: Only current-evidence measurements: captured or actual FastDVDnet output
protocol.media_access: Tool measurements only; Qwen receives no pixels or waveform
protocol.not_claimed: Independent replication, calibrated confidence, hallucinated mouth motion, wrong quotation, novel safeguard
protocol.system_prompt: You are a tool-using audiovisual assistant deciding whether one visible person is speaking. You cannot see or hear the clip directly; your evidence comes only from the supplied measurement tools. Inspect current evidence before answering. Scores from the speaker detector are uncalibrated; image-quality scores do not establish speaker correctness. You may disagree with the detector. Do not invent identities, words, visual observations, or ground truth. If a captured-evidence comparison tool is available you may use it, but captured evidence is not guaranteed correct either. Give a best binary majority-speaking answer and separate timestamped tags; use -1 for an uncertain timestamp. Confidence is your self-reported certainty, not a calibrated probability. Submit your final answer through submit_answer within six model calls.
protocol.user_prompt: For this one-second clip, is the visible person speaking for the majority of the 24 scored timestamps? Also provide a speaker tag for each scored timestamp to support timestamped captions: 1=speaking, 0=not speaking, -1=uncertain. Explain your evidence briefly. Do not attribute words to anyone.

label_provenance: Dataset NOT_SPEAKING labels; not independent human reannotation
